fusion_ranked_evidence.title: Some U.S. schools switch to remote learning, delay start of classes as omicron surge disrupts return from winter break
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # Some U.S. schools switch to remote learning, delay start of classes as omicron surge disrupts return from winter break. Large school districts in Georgia, Michigan, New Jersey, Ohio and Wisconsin are among those whose plans have changed abruptly. Schools across the country have been forced to adapt their plans to return from winter break this week as Covid cases continue to surge. Detroit Public Schools announced on New Year’s Eve that all schools would be closed through at least Wednesday, citing the “city’s all-time high rate of infection at 36 percent.” The district said that it could not offer remote classes Monday because not all students have laptops and that it would announce plans for later in the week. Milwaukee Public Schools said Sunday that they would switch to virtual learning Tuesday because of “an influx of reported positive Covid-19 cases among district staff.” The district said its goal is to resume in-person learning Jan. 10.
